models.scope: durable wake vs committed deadlines, alarm delivery/loss, restart and deploy bootstrap, per-item retry eligibility under a per-wake budget, decision expiry, flow timer rule pin (apps/norn-cell-do/worker.mjs rearm/alarm; crates/norn-api/src/timers.rs next_due/run_due; decisions::expire; flow_turn::timer)

bounds.progressStep: stepProgress: tick and whole passes (fire; oldest-first runItem up to the budget; finish, or a loss after any part of the batch), over the deploy-time cell's items only
bounds.progressDepth: Apalache depth 4 (two alarm deliveries, with a loss at any point) for the intended progress check; seeded simulation of 10,000 traces to depth 15 beyond that; the starvation mutant is refuted at depth 5

assumptions: A1 a cell commit and the durable alarm it registers are one storage transaction (DO storage + setAlarm in one output gate)
A2 alarm delivery is fair: the clock never passes a set alarm by more than FAIR without the alarm firing
A3 at most FAULTS handler losses (eviction, a throw the runtime stops retrying, a crash at any point of a pass) per trace
A4 no logical time passes while one alarm handler runs; writes may interleave with it
A5 an item's handling outcome (healthy or failing) is fixed per incarnation

variants.meaning: Sol blocker 1: the wake is a best-effort rearm after the reply (status-gated, errors swallowed), so a committed deadline can have no wake
Sol blocker 1: the handler re-arms only at its end (after source I/O), so a lost handler leaves due work with no wake
Sol blocker 1: cells from before the deploy hold deadlines but no alarm
Sol blocker 3: expiry records in one transaction and resolves in another; the decision leaves the open set unresolved
Sol should: a flow timer runs the active rule instead of its run's pinned rule
Sol blocker 2: a failed item stops the pass and has no persisted retry time, so the items behind it are never attempted
Sol blocker 2: retry timing is advisory, so failing items refill every batch and a healthy item behind them starves

models.scope: approval digest checked inside the held definition epoch vs a concurrent definition change (crates/norn-api/src/approvals.rs, action_admission.rs, cell_definitions.rs)
assumptions: A1 a definition change takes the definition epoch exclusively; approvals take it for read
A2 the step a call licenses runs under the definition active at its dispatch

variants.meaning: Sol blocker 5 (S6): the digest read releases its epoch before dispatch, so a definition change lands between check and step
Sol blocker 5 (S6): the hosted path still drives the waiting step after answering approval.definition_changed
Sol should: the digest covers the action and writer only, so a change to defaults, law pins or decider roles keeps the approval

notProved: No refinement to the Rust or JavaScript code: the models are the design spec, and no trace from them drives norn-api or the Worker yet (follow-up: a conformance test in the kernel_quint pattern once #1464's fix round lands).
Progress is bounded response under explicit fairness (A2) and a fault budget (A3), checked as invariants to the BMC depth; it is not unbounded LTL liveness with weak fairness.
Bounded: Apalache BMC to the stated depth over three item slots, budget two, logical time 0..7, two calls and two revisions; nothing beyond those bounds is claimed.
Live-law validation at the install boundary (Sol blocker 4), sync scheduling against the global sync lease and the published severity of defs.live_data_unchecked are not modelled.
